spec_role: Changes the tour paradigm from a centralized flashcard deck to game-style contextual popups: when a user enters a module, a spotlight popup appears anchored to the real UI elements on that page, teaching the module's buttons, sub-features, and actions in sequence, then hands off to the next module like a game level. The landed centralized deck (v11.43.0) is demoted to an overview map and re-entry point; the contextual popup tour becomes the primary first-run experience. Supersedes the delivery mechanism of the role_tour_flashcards spec; inherits its content and route-truth laws.

intent: The user's verdict on the landed centralized deck: correct content, wrong delivery. A stack of module cards in one section is a menu, not a tour. Games teach differently: the popup appears where you are, points at the actual button, tells you what it does in one line, waits for you to act or skip, and the next lesson appears at the next place you land. This spec rebuilds the tour that way. When a role enters a module page for the first time, a spotlight popup anchors to the page's real controls (the Collect Fee button, the attendance matrix, the marks-entry table) and walks its steps in order. Finishing or skipping a module's steps marks that module done; the next module's popup fires when the user navigates there, with a progress trail like game level progress. The landed deck data in frontend/src/lib/tours/ is the content source for module and sub-module copy, so nothing is rewritten, only re-delivered in context. The defect class this spec prevents is unchanged: ghost anchors (popups pointing at elements that do not exist), fabricated features, and claimed progress. Every popup anchor is verified against the page's actual markup by an automated test.

honest_caveats: Popup positioning requires DOM anchors. The pages' current markup was not audited element by element at spec time. L0 must inventory each module page's real controls and define the anchor plan; pages may need data-tour attributes added, which is in scope.

Zero new npm dependencies is binding: the spotlight/coach-mark engine is built by hand (overlay, getBoundingClientRect positioning, keyboard, mobile bottom-sheet). No driver.js, shepherd, intro.js, or similar.

Deep pages (for example /school/accounting/reports) are sub-module surfaces; the popup tour covers module landing pages and their highest-value sub-module pages as the L0 matrix decides. Covering every leaf page is not the goal; teaching the jobs is.

scope_boundaries.in_scope_surfaces_rule: The L0 matrix decides which pages get popup tours per role: every module landing page, plus the sub-module pages the matrix marks high-value. Every other page is untouched.

tour_laws.law_1_contextual_trigger: A popup tour step appears only on the page it teaches, triggered by first visit to that page for that role, or by resume/restart from the launcher. No page hosts another page's tour. The centralized deck never auto-opens anymore; it becomes the overview map opened only by the launcher.
tour_laws.law_2_real_anchors: Every step anchors to a real DOM element marked data-tour='{anchor-id}' in the page's markup. A step whose anchor is missing from the page renders nothing and logs a defect; the CI anchor-truth test fails the build if a defined anchor does not exist in the target page source. Ghost popups are the fabricated-truth defect class applied to tours and are prohibited.
tour_laws.law_3_game_sequence: Steps within a page run in defined order with Next/Back, a step counter ('Step 2 of 4'), and a progress trail of modules per role shown as game-style level progress (done / current / locked-by-visit). Completing a module's steps marks that module done; the trail persists; the next module's tour fires when the user first visits it. The trail is shown in the overview deck and inside popups as a compact progress strip.
tour_laws.law_4_skip_everywhere: Skip tour (whole tour, marks all modules dismissed), skip module (marks this module done, moves on), and step-level Next-past are all available on every popup. A skipped tour never auto-opens again on any page. The launcher button always allows revisit, restarting at the first incomplete module or the current page's module.
tour_laws.law_5_act_or_read: Each step's popup states the job in one line ('This button enrolls a student and starts their fee ledger'), what it is, and offers the primary action CTA when the anchor is itself actionable ('Do it now' simply closes the popup so the user can act). Popups never block the underlying control; the user can act while the popup shows, and acting on the anchored control auto-advances the step where detection is reliable, otherwise Next advances.
tour_laws.law_6_honest_copy: Popup copy comes from the landed deck data plus the L0 page audit. A popup must not claim a capability the anchored control lacks. Copy is five-second readable for a tired adult.
tour_laws.law_7_one_engine: One hand-built spotlight/coach-mark engine, one step schema, per-role step definitions as data extending the existing tours/ directory. No per-role copies of the engine. The existing FeatureTutorialFlashCards is refactored into the overview map; nothing is forked.
tour_laws.law_8_mobile_and_a11y: On small viewports popups render as bottom sheets with the anchored element outlined. Keyboard navigation, focus management on open/close, Escape closes the current step (counts as skip module with confirmation), reduced-motion respected, overlay never traps scroll on the taught control.

business_logic_rules: BR-CT-1: Popups fire only on the page they teach, on first visit per role, or via launcher resume. No cross-page popups, no auto-opening deck (law_1).
BR-CT-2: Every step anchors to a real data-tour element verified by the CI anchor-truth test; a popup without its anchor renders nothing and logs a defect (law_2).

BR-CT-3: Progress is a per-role module trail with game-style states (done / current / not-visited), persisted in localStorage under the existing key pattern, resumed on return, never re-shown after dismissal (law_3, law_4).
BR-CT-4: Skip exists at step, module, and tour level on every popup; a skipped tour never auto-opens on any page; the launcher always allows revisit (law_4).
BR-CT-5: Popups never block the anchored control; the user can act underneath; acting auto-advances where detection is reliable (law_5).
BR-CT-6: Copy is honest to the code and five-second readable, drawn from the landed deck data plus the L0 audit (law_6).
BR-CT-7: One hand-built engine, per-role data. Zero new npm dependencies; no third-party tour library (law_7).
BR-CT-8: Telemetry is first-party usage events with role, pagePath, stepId, journey id J10, tenant-scoped, zero PII; north-star definitions untouched.
BR-CT-9: Security unchanged: assertRouteAccess remains the authorization authority; the tour adds no routes, no permissions, no data access; anchor ids are inert markup attributes.
acceptance_criteria: AC-CT-1: docs/product/tour-anchor-matrix.md exists, covers all 11 roles with ordered steps and anchor ids, and was approved by the operator before deck authoring.

AC-CT-2: The spotlight engine renders anchored popups with cutout highlight, step counter, progress strip, Next/Back/Skip, bottom-sheet mode on mobile, keyboard and reduced-motion support, with zero new dependencies.
AC-CT-3: Popups fire contextually on first visit per role per page, never on pages without tour definitions, never again after tour-level dismissal, and resume correctly after refresh.
AC-CT-4: The admin role has contextual tours on its 14 module pages with data-tour anchors on real controls and copy inherited from the landed deck data.
AC-CT-5: The seven staff roles have contextual tours sized honestly to their real surfaces; driver's tour is short and complete for what the driver app does.
AC-CT-6: Parent and student contextual tours work on mobile viewports, in offline states where the host PWA supports them, and never reference admin surfaces.
AC-CT-7: The super-admin tour exists and the provisioning handoff still points new schools' admins at their Day One tour.
AC-CT-8: The CI anchor-truth test passes for every role and demonstrably fails when an anchor is missing or a page is not role-accessible.
AC-CT-9: tour_step_viewed, tour_module_completed, and tour_skipped are emitted tenant-scoped with role, pagePath, and stepId; no north_star event definition changed.
AC-CT-10: The module progress trail persists per role, shows done/current/not-visited states, renders inside popups and the overview deck, and drives resume order.
AC-CT-11: The centralized deck no longer auto-opens; it is the launcher-opened overview map showing the trail; the existing FeatureTutorialFlashCards usages are migrated, not left dangling.

AC-CT-13: Typecheck, build, and smoke render green; keyboard, focus, Escape, and reduced-motion pass across all roles on mobile and desktop.
constraints: Zero new npm dependencies. No driver.js, shepherd, intro.js, react-joyride, or any tour library; the engine is hand-built.
Phases land in strict order CT-L0 through CT-L7, one commit series per layer. Commit prefixes: docs(tour) for L0, feat(tour) for L1 through L7.
Every phase lands with typecheck, build, and smoke render green. The S7 gate is permanent series law.
The L0 anchor matrix is a review gate: the operator approves it before anchors and step data are authored.
Reuse frontend/src/lib/tours/ content and storage patterns; extend types and storage, do not fork them.
Do not modify north-star metric definitions, onboarding wizard steps, or the unified provisioning flow beyond the L5 handoff note.
Where this spec conflicts with in-repo security constraints, security wins; log the conflict in the commit body.
definition_of_done: The contextual tour is done when a first-session user of any of the 11 roles is taught at the moment they open each module: a popup anchors to the module's real buttons, explains the job in one line, lets them act or skip, marks the module done on a persistent game-style progress trail, and the next module's lesson fires when they get there. Every anchor is verified against real page markup by a CI test, every line of copy is honest to what the control does, skip works at step, module, and tour level and is respected forever, and the whole thing is built by hand with zero new dependencies. The centralized deck survives only as the launcher-opened overview map. A new employee at a customer school learns each module while standing in it, without calling anyone.
